# Causal Integrity

> Early AI alignment research hypothesis: whether the causal commitments implicit in purposeful action can ground consistent restraints against causing harm.

Repository: https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity

## Core argument

Purposeful action relies on causal regularity. Communication itself relies on effects being produced and received. Actual causal contributions cannot be erased by an actor's preference. The author proposes that consistently recognizing agency, attribution, and preference pursuit grounds restraints against violating other agents, and seeks an AI that wants to embody those restraints and checks its actions against foreseeable consequences.

At the foundational level, ownership means causal attribution. It must be distinguished from moral responsibility and exclusive property entitlement. Property examples illustrate the argument; conventional property law is not the foundation.

The primary conceptual reference is https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity/blob/main/docs/CONCEPTS.md. Section 5 develops UPB as universalization over action types rather than momentary preferences, together with demonstrated preference and trust collapse.

## Epistemic and implementation status

The full ethical bridge is a hypothesis, not a machine-proven result. The move from pursuing a preference to a universally applicable ethical commitment is a central question. `formalizations/` holds the constructive Lean 4 v2 model `CausalIntegrityV2` (https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity/blob/main/formalizations/CausalIntegrityV2.lean): zero custom axioms, zero `sorry`, stateful non-exclusive attribution, consent/caretaker/competition boundaries, bijective renaming invariance, UPB action-type checks, an executable `allow | reject | escalate` gate, and 15 concrete scenarios. Those theorems are machine-proven consequences of the model's definitions and explicit premises. They do not establish the full philosophical bridge, and real-world deployment remains open. Python examples are illustrations. Self-collapse is an additional stability hypothesis, not the central proof.

The immediate scope is restraints against causing prohibited harm, including foreseeable indirect effects, rather than unlimited positive obligations. The intended AI has an internal commitment to ethical consistency; the work does not claim to prevent every deliberately harmful system.

Superseded earlier-model documents in https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity/blob/main/archive/README.md, including the v1 sketch at https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity/blob/main/archive/formalizations-v1/, are historical drafts, not authoritative. Their terminology and claims need to be read alongside https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity/blob/main/docs/CONCEPTS.md and the README's distinctions between foundation, hypothesis, assumptions, and implementation.
